The recommendation

Buy high-intent suburb search first

Homeowners in The Woodlands, Cypress, Katy, and Spring already type “roof replacement near me” when a leak shows or a storm hits. That search is the closest thing to a warm hand-raise. Social and streaming help later. They do not replace it.

Why suburbs, not the whole metro: Tomball HQ, the Google listing, and the 23 residential city pages already live in this ring — The Woodlands, Cypress, Spring, Katy, Humble, Conroe, Sugar Land, Pearland, League City, and the rest. Paid search should send those homeowners to the matching city page, not a generic Houston ad. Downtown and inside-the-Loop stay out. Austin and Dallas stay out.

Channel mix

Should some budget go to social or streaming?

Yes — but only after Google Search is funded. Homeowners still search first when the roof leaks. Facebook and streaming help because suburban homeowners actually scroll and watch TV at night. They do not replace “roof replacement Cypress TX.”

Yes — starting at $5k/mo

Social: remarketing plus light suburb prospecting

Residential is a better social buy than commercial. Before/after photos, storm damage, and neighborhood geo work on Facebook and Instagram. Still: do not spend the $2k plan on cold social — search has to eat first.

  • $2k: $0 paid social. Keep organic Facebook / Instagram as-is.
  • $5k: ~20% ($1,000) Meta — remarketing of suburb landing-page visitors plus light zip-code prospecting (homeowners 30–64).
  • $10k: ~15% ($1,500) remarketing plus suburb lookalikes. Skip LinkedIn.
  • Creative: shingle replacement, leak repair, hail, before/after, “neighbors in The Woodlands / Katy / Cypress.”
  • Geo-fence the same suburb list as Search. No Austin, no Dallas, no inside-the-Loop.
Yes — only at $10k/mo

Streaming / connected TV: suburb awareness

CTV (YouTube on TV, Google Video on connected devices) is a brand tool for homeowners who watch in the evening. It will not fill the CRM with last-click leads. Use it when search is already running so they later Google “Core Four Roofing” or “roofer in Cypress.”

  • $2k and $5k: $0 CTV. Too little to hit frequency in the suburb zips.
  • $10k: ~10% ($1,000) Houston suburb zips only. 15-second spots, frequency cap 3–4/week.
  • Do not buy Austin, Dallas, or a full DMA dump. Target the same north / west / south ring.
  • Conservative model: zero last-click jobs from CTV. Count a small branded-search lift only.
  • If forced to cut, cut CTV before Search. Search pays for jobs; CTV pays for memory.

How the math stays conservative

Houston residential CPL is often quoted $250–$350. We model higher so the plan still works if auction prices bite.

Search CPC used $24
Click → lead 6.5%
Lead → qualified 70%
Qualified → job (90 days) 18%
All leads → job ~12.6%
Avg residential ticket $14,000
First 30 days CPL +25%
Read the ranges as lumpy, not linear. A $6k leak repair and an $18k replacement both count as “a job.” Storm weeks will spike. Quiet weeks will not. Yearly job counts are what to staff around — not a promise of one signed roof every 30 days.

Where to spend

Houston suburbs. Not the whole map.

Presence targeting (people in or regularly in), not “interested in Houston.” Each ad group sends traffic to the matching residential city page already live. Expand the ring only after the closer-in zips convert.

North ring — start here

Tomball HQ plus The Woodlands, Cypress, Spring, Humble, Atascocita, and Conroe. This is the $2k map. Shortest drive, strongest Google listing, best close rate. 15–20 mile radius from 22955 TX-249.

West — add at $5k

Katy, Fulshear, Richmond, Rosenberg, Sugar Land, Missouri City. Same residential landings, own ad groups, own budgets. Do not mix west keywords into the north campaign.

South / east — add at $10k

Pearland, League City, Friendswood, Pasadena, Baytown, Dickinson. Last ring to turn on. If the $10k budget has to flex, this ring is the first cut — not Tomball search.

Account build

The campaign we would actually run

One Google Ads account, residential only. Brand protected. Suburb search funded. Remarketing catching the researchers. The 23 Houston residential landings you already own. No Performance Max until forms and calls are tracking.

Campaign architecture

Keep suburb rings and intent in separate campaigns so bids cannot leak

Campaign Role Share
Search — Brand Core Four Roofing, misspellings. Cheap, defensive. 5–8%
Search — North suburbs Replacement + repair in Tomball, Woodlands, Cypress, Spring, Humble, Conroe. Core
Search — Storm / hail / leak Emergency and insurance-intent in the same zips. Higher CPC, faster close. Inside core
Search — West / south rings Same themes, own budgets. Off until the $5k / $10k tier. Staged
Local Services Ads Strong for residential roofing in TX. Pay per lead, Google Guaranteed badge. Additive
Remarketing — Display / YouTube 30–90 day residential-page visitors. Estimate CTA. 10%
Meta suburb geo $5k+ only. Remarketing plus homeowner zip targeting. 15–20%
CTV / connected devices $10k only. Suburb zips. Brand + phone. No last-click credit in the model. 10%

Phrase and exact. Tight match. No broad until 50+ conversions.

Negatives from day one: commercial, TPO, EPDM, warehouse, property manager, DIY, jobs, salary, apprentice, free, cheap, metal building kits, Austin, Dallas, and every city Core Four does not serve.

Ads and extensions

RSA headlines that name the suburb (Cypress, The Woodlands, Katy), the job (replacement, leak, hail), and Tomball HQ. Call extension (281) 541-0027. Location, sitelinks to residential city pages, callouts for licensed, insured, local crews. Bid +20% evenings and weekends when homeowners actually search.

Landings already built

Do not send paid traffic to the homepage. Each ad group points at the matching residential city URL — the 23 Houston-metro pages already in Google. Form + click-to-call above the fold. “Free estimate” language is fine here. Keep commercial URLs out of this account.

Tracking before spend

GA4 key events are still at zero on the performance report. Wire form submits, call clicks, and call-tracking numbers, then import offline closes when a job is sold. Without that, we cannot steer budget toward the suburbs that actually become roofs.

First 90 days

How we would turn this on

Start with the north ring even if the long-term budget is $10k. Prove CPL in Tomball / The Woodlands / Cypress / Spring, then add west, then south. Expanding the map before follow-up is tight is how residential budgets disappear.

1

Days 1–14 — plumbing

Conversion tracking, call tracking, negatives for commercial and out-of-area terms, brand campaign, north-suburb search, RSA copy, residential city-page destinations, lead routing to (281) 541-0027 with a same-day callback rule. Start Local Services Ads if Google approves roofing.

2

Days 15–45 — north ring search only

Run 85–90% of budget here. Expect CPL ~25% worse than the model. Cut waste search terms weekly. Turn on Google remarketing once 100+ site visitors exist. No Katy, Pearland, social prospecting, or CTV yet.

3

Days 46–75 — add west + Meta

If north-ring CPL is in range, add Katy / Fulshear / Sugar Land and Meta at the $5k mix. Import sold jobs as offline conversions. Keep Austin and Dallas off.

4

Days 76–90 — scale or hold

If leads are being worked and CPL is under ~$450, step toward $10k: south/east suburbs + CTV. If follow-up is slow or CPL is above $550, stay at $5k north + west — more budget will not fix a leaky sales process.

Best campaign in one line: $5,000/month, 70% Google Search in the Houston suburbs (north ring plus Katy / Sugar Land) to the residential city pages, 10% Google remarketing, 20% Meta in those zips, Austin and Dallas off, CTV off until the $10k tier — with conversion tracking live before the first dollar spends.
